headline: Singapore-based DayOne plans a 200-megawatt data center campus in Imari City, Japan, with the first phase targeted for 2030.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear new project outside Tokyo, but a company announcement with no cost and a 2030 start.
importance_line: Imari City gains an estimated 60 to 80 jobs and Japan gains capacity outside Tokyo, but the plan is DayOne's own and no investment figure is given.
summary: W.Media reports, citing a DayOne press release, that Singapore-based data center company DayOne and Imari City in Saga Prefecture, Japan, announced plans last week for a 200-megawatt campus on a 133,000-square-metre site, with the first phase targeted to open in 2030. DayOne says the campus will employ about 60 to 80 full-time staff and extend its Japan business beyond Tokyo.
notes: The announcement date is given only as 'last week', so no exact date is shown.
